question: Spider naevi are pathological when more than five are found in the distribution of the superior vena cava (above the nipple line), and their presence in a patient with liver disease suggests underlying hyperoestrogenaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The >5 threshold in the SVC distribution distinguishes pathological from incidental spider naevi, and the mechanism in liver disease is hyperoestrogenaemia due to impaired hepatic oestrogen catabolism.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Up to 5 spider naevi may be normal. More than 5 in the SVC distribution (face, neck, upper trunk, arms) is pathological. In chronic liver disease, impaired hepatic oestrogen metabolism leads to hyperoestrogenaemia, which causes arterial dilatation.
